## Executive Summary

> **Purpose**: This white paper defines Spec-Driven Development (SDD) as an industry pattern, surveys the frameworks currently implementing it, and positions Gainwell's own composite model — expressed through a governing decision chain spanning [ADR-GOV-007](../../../decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-007-bdd-testing-methodology.md), [ADR-GOV-009](../../../decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-009-ai-agent-spec-execution-model.md), [ADR-GOV-010](../../../decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-010-ai-agent-label-trigger-control-model.md), and [ADR-GOV-011](../../../decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-011-architecture-pipeline-operating-model.md) (ADR-GOV-007/009/010/011 currently in proposed status, pending ratification) — against that landscape. It is a synthesis paper: it does not re-author the BDD lifecycle, the multi-axis decomposition model, or the agent dispatch pipeline, each of which already has its own governing white paper. It exists to answer a question that recurs across engineering and leadership conversations: **is our accelerator tooling, our spec methodology, and our AI-agent execution model three different things, or one coherent strategy — and how does it compare to what GitHub, AWS, and the open-source community are independently building?**

There is real confusion in the organization today. Teams onboarding a new repository from the enterprise accelerator template encounter Skills, Commands, Prompts, ADRs, BDD `.feature` files, and label-driven agent dispatch simultaneously, with no single document explaining how these pieces relate to a named industry pattern or to each other. Meanwhile, engineers who have used GitHub's Spec Kit, AWS's Kiro, or the independently-run BMAD-METHOD on personal projects reasonably ask why Gainwell has not simply adopted one of them. This paper answers both questions: it names the pattern (Spec-Driven Development), defines its generalized shape, surveys the three most prominent external implementations, and shows that Gainwell's existing governing decision chain is not a delayed or partial version of those tools — it is an independently-derived, more rigorously governed implementation of the same underlying pattern, purpose-built for a regulated healthcare environment none of those external efforts was designed for.

**Key Strategic Points:**

- **Spec-Driven Development is an industry-wide convergent pattern, not a single vendor's product.** An official open-source project owned and maintained by GitHub (GitHub Spec Kit), a commercial hyperscaler product (AWS Kiro), and an independently-governed open-source community project (BMAD-METHOD) all arrived at the same generalized pipeline shape — governance → specification → quality gate → design/plan → task decomposition → autonomous execution → verification → human approval (individual frameworks vary on which gate stages are mandatory versus optional; see §3.2). That three-way convergence is strong evidence this is where the industry is heading, not a speculative bet any one vendor or community is making alone.
- **Gainwell already implements this pattern, expressed as three complementary governing strategies** — BDD as the specification format ([`bdd-lifecycle-strategy.md`](./bdd-lifecycle-strategy.md)), multi-axis contract-first decomposition as the completeness model ([`nodes-and-edges-decomposition-for-agentic-sdlc.md`](./nodes-and-edges-decomposition-for-agentic-sdlc.md)), and label-driven agent dispatch as the execution/governance model ([`ai-agent-sdlc-execution-model.md`](./ai-agent-sdlc-execution-model.md)) — governed end-to-end by a chain of ADRs (see §4.2 for status of individual decisions).
- **Gainwell's approach exceeds the external frameworks on the axis that matters most for this industry**: discrete, supersedable architecture decisions instead of a single embedded file; a pre-engine security screening stage none of the three external frameworks documents; and a dual-system model that preserves regulated audit traceability. It is behind on some execution mechanics (parallel task scheduling, generative property-based testing) that are worth adopting as enhancements, not replacements.
- **Gainwell is positioned to be legible to the outside without diluting its governance on the inside.** A generated, non-authoritative discoverability layer — framework-specific redirects at the exact path each framework actually looks for (Spec Kit's `.specify/memory/`, Kiro's `.kiro/steering/`; BMAD-METHOD already recognizes the accelerator's existing `AGENTS.md`) — turns interoperability into an added strength rather than a gap to close.

### 1.1 Business Context

Every engineering organization adopting AI coding agents eventually confronts the same realization: an agent is only as reliable as the specification it is given. This has produced a wave of tooling — open-source and commercial — organized around the idea that the specification, not the prompt, should be the durable, versioned artifact that drives development. This pattern has acquired a name in the industry: **Spec-Driven Development (SDD)**.

Gainwell arrived at the same conclusion independently, through its own governance process, before benchmarking against external tooling. The result is a governing decision chain — [ADR-GOV-007](../../../decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-007-bdd-testing-methodology.md) (BDD as the behavioral specification standard), [ADR-GOV-009](../../../decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-009-ai-agent-spec-execution-model.md) (the AI Agent Specification Execution Model), [ADR-GOV-010](../../../decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-010-ai-agent-label-trigger-control-model.md) (label-trigger separation of duties), and [ADR-GOV-011](../../../decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-011-architecture-pipeline-operating-model.md) (multi-axis decomposition as the completeness model, with ADR-GOV-007/009/010/011 currently proposed, pending ratification) — plus their technology-tier companions [ADR-TEC-019](../../../decisions/technology/ADR-TEC-019-ai-agent-implementation-decisions.md) and [ADR-TEC-020](../../../decisions/technology/ADR-TEC-020-ai-coding-assistant-construct-taxonomy.md) (both also currently proposed, pending ratification). Individually, each decision and its companion white paper is well-documented. Collectively, they have never been named as what they are: Gainwell's implementation of Spec-Driven Development.

**Key Business Drivers:**

- Engineering teams evaluating or already using external SDD tooling (GitHub Spec Kit, AWS Kiro) need a clear, honest comparison to Gainwell's own model — not a directive to avoid external tools, and not silence that implies Gainwell has nothing comparable
- Leadership and the Architecture Review Board need a single reference that states what SDD is, why Gainwell's approach takes the shape it does, and what risk or opportunity is associated with the current external tooling landscape
- New teams onboarding through the enterprise accelerator encounter Skills, Commands, ADRs, BDD specs, and agent dispatch simultaneously, with no single document connecting these mechanisms to the named industry pattern they collectively implement
- Absence of a definitional anchor risks fragmentation — individual teams reaching for external tools piecemeal, recreating governance capability Gainwell has already established, in a form that is less auditable for a HIPAA-scoped environment

### 1.2 Strategic Scope

This white paper focuses on:

- **Definition**: What Spec-Driven Development is, expressed as a generalized, tool-agnostic workflow
- **Landscape**: The external frameworks currently implementing this pattern, and what each one does well
- **Composition**: How Gainwell's three existing, governing strategies compose into the same pattern, without duplicating their content
- **Positioning**: Why Gainwell's divergence from the external frameworks is deliberate, and where Gainwell is positioned relative to an industry that has not yet settled on a single standard

> **Boundary note**: This paper does not redefine BDD authoring, multi-axis decomposition, or agent dispatch mechanics — those remain owned by their respective white papers. It also does not recommend adopting any specific external tool. Where external tools are named (GitHub Spec Kit, AWS Kiro), they are referenced as illustrative, independently-verifiable evidence of an industry pattern, consistent with how this series treats named tools elsewhere.

### 2.1 Problem Statement

Three distinct concepts are routinely conflated in conversation, and each conflation causes a different organizational cost:

1. **The accelerator template repository** (the reusable scaffold that bootstraps a new product repository with Skills, Commands, Prompts, and CI/CD conventions) is a *delivery mechanism*.
2. **Spec-Driven Development** (governance → spec → gate → design/plan → decomposition → execution → verification) is a *methodology* — a way of structuring how work is specified and built, independent of which repository or tool implements it.
3. **AI coding agents** (Copilot, Claude Code, or any specialized implementation/documentation/testing/infrastructure agent) are the *executing actors* that the methodology governs and the accelerator wires into a pipeline.

Without a document that separates these three, engineers reasonably ask "why doesn't our accelerator just install Spec Kit?" — a question that conflates a delivery mechanism with a methodology, and a methodology with a specific vendor's implementation of it.

**What's at Stake:**

- Duplicated or shadow adoption of external SDD tooling by individual teams, outside architecture governance, in a regulated environment where spec content and agent execution boundaries are compliance-relevant
- Erosion of confidence in the existing ADR chain if it is perceived as "not really SDD" simply because it does not use industry terminology
- Missed opportunity to present Gainwell's model, externally or to leadership, as a mature and in some respects more rigorous implementation of a pattern the rest of the industry is still stabilizing

### 2.2 Impact on the Organization

**Current State Challenges:**

- No single artifact currently uses the term "Spec-Driven Development" to connect [ADR-GOV-007](../../../decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-007-bdd-testing-methodology.md), [ADR-GOV-009](../../../decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-009-ai-agent-spec-execution-model.md) through [ADR-GOV-012](../../../decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-012-forward-only-change-propagation-and-execution-idempotency.md), and the three companion white papers into one coherent story
- Engineers encountering GitHub Spec Kit or AWS Kiro externally have no reference point for how those tools' concepts (`constitution.md`, `requirements.md`/`design.md`/`tasks.md`) map to Gainwell's own concepts (ADRs, `.feature` files, seam contracts, labeled issues)
- Leadership asking "are we behind the industry on AI-driven development?" currently receives an implicit answer scattered across multiple ADRs and three white papers rather than one direct comparison

**Why Current Approaches Fall Short:**

Each existing white paper is deliberately scoped to one pipeline stage and correctly avoids external tool comparison to stay technically precise. That precision is the right choice for those documents, but it leaves a gap: nothing currently answers the landscape-level question at the altitude leadership and new engineers actually ask it.

[strategy/white-papers/engineering/spec-driven-development-strategy.md#31-the-generalized-workflow] ### 3.1 The Generalized Workflow Stripped of any single vendor's command names, Spec-Driven Development is an agentic SDLC pattern with **gates between artifact tiers**, where the specification — not the prompt — is the durable, versioned, auditable artifact. This paper's own survey (§3.2) finds individual frameworks vary on which gates are mandatory versus optional — Spec Kit's and Kiro's completeness checks are optional, and BMAD-METHOD permits small changes to route directly to Build; what the three frameworks converge on is the *staged shape* below, not universal gate enforcement. Gainwell's own composite model (§4.0) makes every gate mandatory by deliberate choice, not because the industry survey requires it: ```mermaid flowchart LR A["Governance
(durable principles +
system boundary/decisions)"] B["Specification
(WHAT/WHY, stable IDs)"] C["Quality Gate
(completeness/consistency
check — blocks forward flow)"] D["Design/Plan
(research, architecture,
interfaces, test conditions)"] E["Decomposition
(spec mapped to discrete,
executable tasks)"] F["Autonomous Execution
(agent produces code against
the plan — not the raw spec)"] G["Verification
(traceability/conformance,
fitness, or property checks)"] H["Human Approval
(review, merge, release)"] A --> B --> C --> D --> E --> F --> G --> H ``` The defining characteristic of SDD, as distinct from ad-hoc AI-assisted coding, is that **each stage's output gates the next**: an agent is not permitted to plan against an unclarified spec, and is not permitted to execute against an unapproved plan. This is the same "fail fast at the cheapest stage" discipline CI/CD introduced for code, applied one layer earlier — to specification and design.

### 3.2 Frameworks Implementing This Pattern

Three independent efforts, from very different origins, have converged on this same generalized shape:

**GitHub Spec Kit** (`github.com/github/spec-kit`) — an open-source toolkit owned and maintained by GitHub (a Microsoft subsidiary) under its own organization account, MIT-licensed, with a large and active outside contributor community alongside GitHub's own maintainers. Its core loop — `/speckit.constitution` → `/speckit.specify` → `/speckit.plan` → `/speckit.tasks` → `/speckit.implement` → `/speckit.converge` — implements the generalized workflow directly, with optional gates (`/speckit.clarify`, `/speckit.checklist`, `/speckit.analyze`) for ambiguity resolution and cross-artifact traceability. A community-maintained preset (`spec-kit-workflow-preset`, and its now-retired predecessor `spec-kit-arch`) extends the core with a governance/architecture split: a `constitution.md` for durable principles and a single `architecture.md` covering system boundary, conceptual model, technical decisions, and planning gaps — notably, without a multi-viewpoint architecture model or a discrete, individually-supersedable decision registry.

**AWS Kiro** (`kiro.dev`) — a commercial, enterprise-supported agentic IDE and CLI from AWS. Its "specs" follow a three-phase workflow — `requirements.md` (user stories + acceptance criteria) → `design.md` (architecture, sequence diagrams, test strategy) → `tasks.md` (dependency-graphed, execution in parallel waves) — with an optional `Analyze Requirements` consistency gate before design, and a distinctive verification mechanism: requirement-tied, generative property-based testing (assertions that must hold across all inputs, not just enumerated examples).

**BMAD-METHOD** (`github.com/bmad-code-org/BMAD-METHOD`) — "Breakthrough Method for Agile AI-Driven Development," an independent, MIT-licensed open-source project with a large and active community, iterating through major versions at a rapid pace. Rather than a single-agent command sequence, it composes multiple specialized planning personas (Analyst, Product Manager, Architect, Developer, UX Designer) — with Test Architect available as a separately-selected optional add-on module (`defaultSelected: false` in `bmad-modules.yaml`; not included in the default agent set) that produce the same durable artifact tier as the other two frameworks — a PRD, an architecture document, and per-story task specs — through a named loop: *Clarify → Plan → Build and verify → Learn and adjust*, looping back to Plan. Notably, its Analyst persona performs market research, brainstorming, and project-brief elicitation as a discovery activity preceding the PM's PRD — a discovery gate neither GitHub Spec Kit nor AWS Kiro formalizes (see §4.1's Discovery row for how Gainwell treats this same activity). Its "right-sized process" principle lets small changes skip straight to Build while complex work receives full multi-persona planning, and its ecosystem includes a dedicated test-architecture add-on and an unattended "BMad Loop" mode for building, verifying, and retrospecting a full epic without a human in the loop at each stage.

None of the three frameworks addresses dual-system governance (an execution surface synchronized with a regulated, sprint-governed system of record) — that is a Gainwell-specific requirement none of them was built to solve, and it is the primary contribution of [`ai-agent-sdlc-execution-model.md`](./ai-agent-sdlc-execution-model.md).

> **Adjacent, but not a peer**: `AGENTS.md` — an open, vendor-neutral convention for agent context files, now stewarded by the Agentic AI Foundation under the Linux Foundation and adopted broadly across open-source repositories (with contributions from OpenAI, Google, Cursor, and Factory) — validates convergence at the *context/instruction* layer (relevant to [ADR-TEC-020](../../../decisions/technology/ADR-TEC-020-ai-coding-assistant-construct-taxonomy.md)'s construct taxonomy), not at the gated spec→plan→tasks pipeline layer these three frameworks implement. It is cited here for completeness, not counted as a fourth SDD framework.

### 3.3 Expected Outcomes of a Shared Definition

**Strategic Benefits:**

- A single, shared vocabulary ends the false choice between "adopt an external tool" and "we have nothing like that" — the organization can state precisely what it has, in industry terms, and what it deliberately does differently
- New engineers and leadership gain one reference document that maps Gainwell's ADR chain onto terms they may already recognize from external tooling
- Architecture governance gains a standing artifact to evaluate future external SDD tooling against, rather than re-deriving the comparison ad hoc each time a new tool is proposed

**Success Indicators:**

- Engineers evaluating external SDD tools reference this paper before proposing adoption, rather than raising the question in isolation
- The Architecture Review Board uses this paper's framework to assess any future external SDD tool proposal against the same generalized workflow and the same divergence rationale

## 4.0 Gainwell's Composite Model — How the Three Pillars Compose

[strategy/white-papers/engineering/spec-driven-development-strategy.md#41-mapping-the-pillars-to-the-generalized-workflow]

### 4.1 Mapping the Pillars to the Generalized Workflow

Gainwell's model is not a single tool — it is three governing strategies that together cover every stage of the generalized workflow in §3.1:

| Generalized stage | Owning Gainwell strategy | What it contributes |
|---|---|---|
| Discovery | [GUID-GOV-PROC-011](../../guidance/governance/processes/GUID-GOV-PROC-011-requirements-engineering-regulated-domains.md) (Requirements Engineering for Regulated Domains) | Capability elicitation, regulatory/legacy requirement derivation, and as-is reverse engineering — the raw material Specification operationalizes into executable scenarios |
| Governance | This paper + the ADR chain (§4.2) | Discrete, numbered, independently-supersedable architecture decisions — not a single embedded file |
| Specification | [`bdd-lifecycle-strategy.md`](./bdd-lifecycle-strategy.md) | Gherkin `.feature` files as the single source of truth, authored via AI-assisted decomposition from business requirement to executable scenario |
| Quality gate / completeness | [`nodes-and-edges-decomposition-for-agentic-sdlc.md`](./nodes-and-edges-decomposition-for-agentic-sdlc.md) | Multi-axis, contract-first decomposition — behavior, seam, negative property, non-functional, data, journey — closing the gap plain BDD leaves for autonomous agents |
| Design/Plan | Standards and patterns referenced by ADR-GOV-011 (seam contracts, AsyncAPI, JSON Schema, OPA/Rego, Arazzo) | Design-time artifacts in recognized industry standards, treated as binding build inputs rather than after-the-fact documentation |
| Decomposition / routing | [`ai-agent-sdlc-execution-model.md`](./ai-agent-sdlc-execution-model.md) | Label taxonomy (`agent-task` + `agent:<type>`) routing to specialized agent pipelines |
| Autonomous execution | [`ai-agent-sdlc-execution-model.md`](./ai-agent-sdlc-execution-model.md) | Validate → Dispatch → Report pipeline; agent output is a pull request, never a direct commit |
| Verification | ADR-GOV-011/012 + branch protection | Merge-blocking verification gates per axis; forward-only, idempotent change propagation |
| Human approval | Dual-system sync contract | Enterprise work item cross-reference is a pipeline gate; PR review remains a human checkpoint |
| Cross-tool discoverability | Generated compatibility layer (accelerator tooling; ADR ratification recommended in §7.0) | Non-authoritative, framework-specific redirects — Spec Kit core's `.specify/memory/constitution.md` and the community Workflow Preset's `.specify/memory/architecture.md`, Kiro's `.kiro/steering/` — into the ADR chain, design docs, and BDD specs; never a second source of truth, and never a one-size-fits-all file set |

Gainwell treats Discovery as a necessary input to Specification, not an optional convenience — every specification is expected to trace to a capability inventory entry, a derived requirement candidate, or an as-is reverse-engineered rule, rather than being authored from an unrecorded conversation. BMAD-METHOD reaches the same conclusion independently with its dedicated Analyst persona (§3.2). GitHub Spec Kit and AWS Kiro do not require it: both accept intent directly at their Specification stage (`/speckit.specify`, `requirements.md`) with no gated elicitation activity of their own — which is why [PTN-TEC-AI-005](../../../patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-005-spec-driven-development-composition-pattern.md) documents Discovery as an optional Variation rather than a mandatory stage.

[strategy/white-papers/engineering/spec-driven-development-strategy.md#42-the-governing-decision-chain]

### 4.2 The Governing Decision Chain

Unlike any of the three external frameworks surveyed in §3.2, Gainwell's model is expressed as a chain of individually-authored, cross-referencing ADRs rather than a single configuration file (all currently in proposed status, pending ratification; each can be independently revisited or superseded once ratified):

- [ADR-GOV-007](../../../decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-007-bdd-testing-methodology.md) — BDD as the behavioral specification standard
- [ADR-GOV-009](../../../decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-009-ai-agent-spec-execution-model.md) — the AI Agent Specification Execution Model (issue tracker as execution queue)
- [ADR-GOV-010](../../../decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-010-ai-agent-label-trigger-control-model.md) — separation-of-duties control on who may trigger agent dispatch
- [ADR-GOV-011](../../../decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-011-architecture-pipeline-operating-model.md) — multi-axis decomposition and foundation-before-fan-out as the completeness model
- [ADR-GOV-012](../../../decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-012-forward-only-change-propagation-and-execution-idempotency.md) — forward-only change propagation and execution idempotency
- [ADR-TEC-019](../../../decisions/technology/ADR-TEC-019-ai-agent-implementation-decisions.md) / [ADR-TEC-020](../../../decisions/technology/ADR-TEC-020-ai-coding-assistant-construct-taxonomy.md) — implementation decisions and the cross-tool construct taxonomy (Skills, Agents, Commands, Prompts)

Each decision can be individually revisited, superseded, or extended without invalidating the others — the structural property Spec Kit core's `constitution.md` (and the community Workflow Preset's `architecture.md`) do not provide, since neither file is independently supersedable within its own artifact.

## 5.0 Why Gainwell's Approach Diverges — and Why That Is Deliberate

Gainwell's model diverges from all three external frameworks in specific, intentional ways, each traceable to a requirement of operating in a regulated healthcare environment:

- **Discrete ADRs instead of a single architecture file** — supports independent supersession, audit history, and per-decision review, which a flat `architecture.md` or `constitution.md` cannot express, and which BMAD-METHOD's PRD/architecture document pair does not provide either
- **A pre-engine security screening stage** ([ADR-TEC-019](../../../decisions/technology/ADR-TEC-019-ai-agent-implementation-decisions.md), decision D5) — regex-based injection and PHI screening runs before any spec content reaches a model, a control none of the three external frameworks documents as a discrete governed stage
- **Separation-of-duties on the execution trigger** ([ADR-GOV-010](../../../decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-010-ai-agent-label-trigger-control-model.md)) — the actor who authors a spec may not be the actor who fires its execution, a control with no analog in any of the three external frameworks
- **A dual-system model that preserves the regulated system of record** — the issue tracker is the execution surface; the enterprise work management system remains authoritative for compliance, sprint governance, and stakeholder reporting. None of the three external frameworks addresses this split because none of them operates under this constraint
- **Multi-axis decomposition** ([ADR-GOV-011](../../../decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-011-architecture-pipeline-operating-model.md)) — extending beyond behavior-only specs to seams, negative properties, and shared foundations, addressing a failure mode (silently unbuilt integration edges) that none of the three frameworks' documentation discusses

> **Note on framework-specific redirects**: Gainwell does generate artifacts recognizable to individual external frameworks — e.g., a redirect at Spec Kit core's `.specify/memory/constitution.md` path and, for teams using the community Workflow Preset, at its `.specify/memory/architecture.md` path; and one at Kiro's expected `.kiro/steering/` path. These are generated pointers into the ADR chain and BDD specs described above, at each framework's own path and name — never a single generic file set imitating all three at once, and never a parallel governance model. Discoverability is additive; the divergence in this section is unchanged.

Where Gainwell's model is currently less mature than the external frameworks, the gap is in execution mechanics, not governance:

- Neither the dispatch pipeline nor the BDD lifecycle currently specifies dependency-graph-based **parallel task execution**, which Kiro implements
- Gainwell's verification model relies on branch protection and (as a target state) architecture conformance gates; it does not yet specify **generative property-based testing** tied to requirement IDs, which Kiro implements as a distinct verification layer
- Gainwell's model does not currently offer a **right-sized process escape hatch** for small changes — BMAD-METHOD's ability to route trivial work straight to Build while reserving full multi-persona planning for complex work is worth evaluating against the label-taxonomy routing in [`ai-agent-sdlc-execution-model.md`](./ai-agent-sdlc-execution-model.md)

These are candidate enhancements to evaluate against the existing roadmap phases in [`ai-agent-sdlc-execution-model.md`](./ai-agent-sdlc-execution-model.md) — not evidence that the underlying model needs to change.

## 6.0 Positioning for Industry Leadership

No single framework — open-source or commercial — has yet become the de facto industry standard for Spec-Driven Development. GitHub Spec Kit remains a young, fast-evolving project; AWS Kiro is a commercial product still expanding its enterprise governance surface; BMAD-METHOD is a fast-moving community project iterating through major versions at a rapid pace; the community extensions attempting to add enterprise-grade architecture governance to Spec Kit (`spec-kit-arch`, `spec-kit-workflow-preset`) are single-maintainer efforts that have already gone through a significant rewrite. The pattern is converging; the standard is not yet settled.

This is Gainwell's opportunity. The organization is not late to Spec-Driven Development — it independently arrived at the same pattern through its own governance process, and on the specific dimension the industry has not yet solved (auditable governance for regulated environments), Gainwell's governing ADR chain is further along than any of the three external frameworks. Three conditions support a leadership position rather than a follower position:

1. **The governance gap is real and unsolved industry-wide.** None of the three external frameworks has a discrete ADR-equivalent registry, a pre-engine security screening stage, or a dual-system regulated-record model. A regulated-industry SDD reference model is a genuine, currently-unclaimed contribution Gainwell is positioned to make.
2. **The pattern is stable enough to commit to, not so settled that Gainwell would be entering late.** Convergent evolution across an open-source vendor project (GitHub/Microsoft), a hyperscaler, and an independent open-source community validates the shape without requiring Gainwell to wait for a single winner to emerge.
3. **Gainwell's model is already expressed as structured, durable artifacts** (ADRs, patterns, standards) rather than tribal practice — the form external standards bodies and industry publications engage with, should Gainwell choose to publish or contribute this model externally.

Leadership in this context does not require building a competing public toolkit. It means: naming the pattern internally, continuing to harden the governance dimensions that already exceed external tooling, selectively adopting external execution mechanics worth borrowing (§5.0), and — when the organization is ready — publishing the governance model (not the internal implementation) as a contribution to the industry's still-forming standard.

A generated discoverability layer is a concrete example of this stance: it lets a project surface a recognizable entry point at the exact path each framework's own tooling actually looks for — Spec Kit's `.specify/memory/`, Kiro's `.kiro/steering/` — without asking Gainwell's governance model to imitate any of them, and without pretending a single generic file set could ever speak all three languages at once. That combination — legible to the outside, undiluted on the inside — is precisely what a leadership position looks like before the industry has settled on a standard.

### Immediate Priorities

1. **Adopt "Spec-Driven Development" as the named internal term for this composite model**

    - Reference this paper from the three companion white papers and from onboarding material for the enterprise accelerator template
    - Key stakeholders: Enterprise Architecture Practice, Platform Engineering

2. **Ratify a discoverability-layer capability as governed practice, not an ungoverned convenience**

    - Accelerator tooling can already generate non-authoritative artifacts that redirect into the real ADR chain and BDD specs for cross-tool recognizability. Author a lightweight ADR recording this decision so this paper can cite it as ratified rather than as tooling that happens to exist
    - Key stakeholders: Enterprise Architecture Practice

3. **Use this paper as the standing evaluation framework for any proposed external SDD tool adoption**

    - Any future proposal to adopt GitHub Spec Kit, AWS Kiro, or a similar framework should be evaluated against §4 and §5 of this paper before an ARB decision is requested
    - Key stakeholders: Architecture Review Board, Solutions Architects

### 8.1 Strategic Imperative

The industry question is no longer whether specifications should be the durable artifact driving AI-assisted development — independent convergence across open-source and commercial tooling has settled that question. The open question is whose governance model earns trust in regulated environments first. Gainwell already has a credible answer, expressed across a chain of ADRs and three companion white papers; what has been missing is the single document connecting them to the term the rest of the industry now uses to describe this pattern.
page_texts.25:
[strategy/white-papers/engineering/spec-driven-development-strategy.md#82-call-to-action]

### 8.2 Call to Action

**Recommended Next Steps:**

1. Enterprise Architecture Practice socializes this paper with engineering leadership and the Architecture Review Board as the definitional anchor for Spec-Driven Development at Gainwell
2. Any team currently considering ad hoc adoption of an external SDD tool reviews §4 and §5 of this paper first, and routes the proposal through the Architecture Review Board if a genuine gap is identified
3. Platform Engineering evaluates the two specific execution-mechanics gaps in §5.0 as scoped enhancements to the existing roadmap, on the existing implementation cadence

**The Strategic Message**: Gainwell did not adopt Spec-Driven Development from the outside — it arrived at the same pattern independently, through its own governance discipline, and on the dimension that matters most for this industry, it is already ahead.

### If a Dominant External Standard Emerges

Should the industry converge on a single dominant SDD toolkit or file format (rather than the current plurality of GitHub Spec Kit, AWS Kiro, and community extensions), Gainwell should evaluate interoperability — e.g., whether Gherkin `.feature` files or ADR content could be exported to that standard's format — rather than migrating its governance model wholesale. Gainwell's accelerator-level discoverability layer (pending ADR ratification per §7.0) is the natural extension point for that interoperability posture — extending it, rather than replacing the governance model underneath, should be the default response if a dominant standard emerges.
page_texts.28:
[strategy/white-papers/engineering/spec-driven-development-strategy.md#contribution-back-to-the-industry]

### Contribution Back to the Industry

If Gainwell's governance model (discrete ADR chain, pre-engine security screening, dual-system regulated record) proves durable in production, publishing it as an enterprise reference pattern — through an industry conference presentation, a public pattern contribution, or a whitepaper — is a credible path to the leadership positioning described in §6.0.

### Continued Convergence Monitoring

This paper's §3.2 landscape survey should be revisited at minimum semi-annually — the external landscape has already shown it can shift shape quickly (rapid release cadence, at least one full architecture-model rewrite among the surveyed frameworks) — a stale comparison would mislead rather than inform.

[strategy/white-papers/engineering/spec-driven-development-strategy.md#strategy-summary-tldr]

## Strategy Summary (TL;DR)

**Strategic Challenge:** Teams conflate the accelerator template, Spec-Driven Development as a methodology, and AI coding agents as executing actors — creating confusion, risking shadow adoption of external tools, and obscuring that Gainwell's own governing ADR chain already implements the same industry pattern GitHub Spec Kit and AWS Kiro independently converged on.

**Proposed Approach:** Name the pattern, define its generalized workflow, map Gainwell's three existing composite strategies (BDD lifecycle, multi-axis decomposition, agent dispatch) onto it, and show precisely where Gainwell's governance model exceeds external tooling and where specific execution mechanics are worth borrowing.

**Expected Impact:** A single reference document that ends ad hoc external-tool debates, gives the Architecture Review Board a standing evaluation framework, and positions Gainwell to claim leadership on regulated-environment SDD governance once the broader industry's standard consolidates.
